guarantees.claim: sp2v_sig[0] is driven by state_we_ctrl, sp2v_sig[1] by key_full_we_ctrl, and sp2v_sig[2] by key_dec_we_ctrl
Sp2VEnSecBuf is set to all ones, statically enabling security buffering for all three sp2v signals

assumptions.claim: Input signals state_we_ctrl, key_full_we_ctrl, key_dec_we_ctrl must provide valid dual-rail encoded values consistent with the sp2v_e type
assumptions.cond: during any clock cycle where these signals are used for downstream single-rail conversion
assumptions.risk: Invalid dual-rail encoding could cause incorrect single-rail conversion, leading to unauthorized state or key register writes and potential leakage of secrets

uncertain_points.claim: sp2v_sig_err is declared as a 3-bit error flag but is not driven in this region; if it remains undriven elsewhere, dual-rail encoding violations may go undetected
uncertain_points.cond: if sp2v_sig_err is never assigned a value
uncertain_points.risk: Loss of fault detection for dual-rail errors could allow compromised control signals to silently trigger illegal write operations, breaking AES security

uncertain_points.claim: Sp2VEnSecBuf is hard-coded to all ones, providing no per-signal override to disable security buffering; the design intent for this static enable is unclear
uncertain_points.risk: Unnecessary power/area consumption or masking of design errors if some signals do not require security buffering

uncertain_points.claim: sp2v_sig_chk and sp2v_sig_chk_raw are declared but not connected in this region; their intended purpose as dual-rail check values is unknown and may be left floating
uncertain_points.cond: unknown where these signals are driven and used
uncertain_points.risk: The dual-rail conversion check might be incomplete or bypassed, reducing fault-injection resistance
